clue.text: Be good enough to give policemen hearty meals

definitions.meaning: to be just what is required, adequate to the task
read literally: to stuff 'the Bill', British slang for the police, with food

explanation.surface: Someone proves their worth by feeding the local constabulary generously.
explanation.walkthrough: THE BILL is British slang for the police (also a long-running TV police drama), so filling it is feeding officers.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning to be exactly what is needed, to suffice.

clue.text: Iron-clad barge designed by a famous jeweller

indicators.note: clad means clothed or wrapped, so the iron symbol encloses the other letters

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: designed means newly arranged, so the letters of barge are reworked

explanation.surface: An armoured boat has been created by a celebrated maker of jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron-clad' reads as armoured, describing the barge; split it, and the iron symbol is what does the cladding. 'designed' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Fabergé was the Russian goldsmith famed for his jewelled imperial eggs.

clue.text: See purpose in a parasitic insect

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or see
use means purpose, as in 'what is the use?'

explanation.surface: Someone notices a reason for a bug's existence.
explanation.definitionFit: A wingless bloodsucking pest living on the hair or skin of animals.

clue.text: Rebuked for having marked all the boxes

definitions.meaning: scolded, told off sharply
literally, every item on a list has been checked off with a tick

explanation.surface: Someone is scolded after filling in every square on a form.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal phrase for reprimanded; literally, items checked off one by one.

clue.text: Islamic leader appears as the hoar-frost returns

indicators.note: returns means the frost word comes back, read from right to left

parts.note: rime is a white frost formed on cold surfaces

explanation.surface: A Muslim ruler shows up when winter frost comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns RIME round to give the ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A title for a Muslim ruler or commander, as in the Gulf states.

clue.text: Took a deep breath when filled with creative energy

definitions.meaning: breathed in, the literal sense of the verb
stimulated by genius or a muse

explanation.surface: An artist gasps when a burst of creativity strikes.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means inhaled; the adjective means moved by artistic genius.

clue.text: Tether for the French tree

parts.note: le is the French masculine for 'the'
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: A rope ties something to a tree in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap or lead used for restraining a dog or other animal.

clue.text: Dead in bed, and none too soon

indicators.note: in places the word for deceased within the word for bed

parts.note: late means deceased, as in 'the late king'

explanation.surface: Someone found dead in bed, and the discovery came rather late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal: the word for dead goes inside the word for bed, which is split after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming later than expected or than it should; tardy.

clue.text: Put forward the case against the kilo?

definitions.meaning: to propose or offer for consideration
being in favour of the imperial pound weight is arguing against the metric kilogram

explanation.surface: Someone presents the argument against metric weights.
explanation.definitionFit: To offer an idea or theory for others to consider.

clue.text: Conservative old schoolmaster comes from good stock

parts.note: blue is the colour of the UK Conservative Party
Mr Chips is the old schoolmaster in James Hilton's novel Goodbye, Mr Chips

explanation.surface: A traditionalist veteran teacher has a fine family background.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good stock' looks like breeding, but here it means safe shares on the stock market.
explanation.definitionFit: Shares in large, reliable companies are known on the market by this name.

clue.text: A couple I left in springtime

parts.note: pr is the abbreviation for pair

explanation.surface: A pair and I set off in the spring.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth month falls in the spring season of the northern hemisphere.

clue.text: Midshipman's joint

definitions.meaning: old naval slang for a junior officer, who reefed the sails
slang for a cannabis cigarette

explanation.surface: A junior naval officer has a cannabis cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Naval slang for a junior officer; also slang for a cannabis cigarette.

clue.text: The best part of a holiday in the mountains

definitions.meaning: the most enjoyable moment of an experience

definitions.text: of a holiday in the mountains
definitions.meaning: read literally as an elevated location

explanation.surface: Describing the most memorable moment of a trip to the hills.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for the outstanding moment of an event; literally an elevated place.

clue.text: Use typical measure and manoeuvre

parts.note: an em is a printer's unit of measurement, typical here hinting at type
a ploy is a cunning manoeuvre

explanation.surface: A tactic involving a standard measurement is put into practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'typical' means 'of type': the em is a typesetter's unit.
explanation.definitionFit: To make use of, or to engage someone for work.

clue.text: Quietly takes a new violin from the summer-house

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: new signals the letters of a violin are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone softly removes a brand-new violin from a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges A and VIOLIN into AVILION, after P.
explanation.definitionFit: A light ornamental building in a garden, used in summer.

clue.text: Stay on the move, or else become fat

definitions.meaning: keep travelling about from place to place
read literally: to grow round in shape

explanation.surface: Keep moving or else you'll put on weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb for travelling widely; literally to turn plump.

clue.text: Dealings accounts

definitions.meaning: contacts between parties
narratives or tellings, as in the relation of a story

explanation.surface: A bare pairing of business transactions and reports.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both connections between groups and narratives of events.

clue.text: A high-ranking detective in need of LSD

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British plain-clothes police
head as in head boy, the top-ranking

explanation.surface: A senior police detective wants some drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition names a habitual taker of the drug LSD; in old Britain LSD also meant pounds, shillings and pence, so 'in need of money' lurks.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a habitual user of hallucinogenic drugs.

clue.text: Apply protective cosmetics to maintain self-esteem

definitions.meaning: read literally: to preserve one's complexion
to avoid humiliation or loss of dignity

explanation.surface: Wear skincare to keep up your pride.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for avoiding embarrassment; literally, preserving one's complexion.

clue.text: It's heavenly under the linden tree

parts.note: sub is Latin for under
the lime is another name for the linden tree

explanation.surface: It feels divine to sit beneath the lime tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Of supreme excellence or beauty, transcendent.

clue.text: An unmotivated flier?

parts.note: unmotivated read as 'without a motor': an aircraft that flies with no engine

explanation.surface: Describing a lazy, uninspired pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unmotivated' looks like lazy, but it means having no motor.
explanation.definitionFit: An engineless aircraft that rides air currents.

clue.text: Communists clearly have the edge in producing paint pigment

parts.note: reds are communists, after their flag colour
to lead is to be ahead, to have the edge

explanation.surface: Communists are plainly winning the race to make paint.
explanation.definitionFit: A red oxide of lead, formerly used in protective paints.

clue.text: Capital needed to refurbish regal bed

indicators.note: refurbish means do up, so the letters of regal bed are rebuilt

explanation.surface: Money is required to renovate a royal bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to refurbish' rearranges REGAL BED. 'Capital' looks like money but is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Serbia.

clue.text: An extract of pine? Wrong again!

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: Someone takes a piece of pine and regrets erring once more.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticky substance exuded by pine and other trees.

clue.text: String of beads by the beach

definitions.meaning: a single thread of beads, as in a necklace
the shore, especially in older usage

explanation.surface: A necklace is found by the seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a thread or string and the shore.

clue.text: A barrier built of stone

parts.note: a gate is a barrier across an opening

explanation.surface: A wall is constructed out of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A banded variety of chalcedony, a semi-precious stone.

clue.text: A young animal to show sa much affection

definitions.meaning: a young deer in its first year
to be servilely affectionate, like a fond dog

explanation.surface: A baby creature is very loving.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a young deer and to flatter servilely.

clue.text: Shackles the star of The Mission'

definitions.meaning: fetters or chains for prisoners
Jeremy ... starred in the 1986 film The Mission

explanation.surface: Chains for the lead actor of a film.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means fetters and is the surname of an actor.

clue.text: To give further details is complicated

definitions.meaning: to expand on something
intricate, highly detailed

explanation.surface: Expanding an explanation makes it intricate.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to expand upon; the adjective means intricate.

clue.text: So had no need, anyhow, to give assent

indicators.note: anyhow means in a careless, haphazard way, so the letters of so had no need are jumbled

explanation.surface: There was no need to agree after all.
explanation.definitionFit: To move one's head up and down as a sign of agreement.
